Brazil Congress Approves Shorter Workweek

Brazil's Congress has approved a bill reducing the standard workweek from 44 to 40 hours, mandating two paid days off instead of the current one. The measure, which the government had been advocating for months, received support from Flavio Bolsonaro, who reversed his previous stance and backed the end of a six-day workweek. President Lula is reportedly counting on the bill's passage to gain political ground ahead of upcoming elections.
